entries.title: II Kings 8:1
segments: When the Lord is about to chastise a people for their sins, he remembers his children and supplies their wants or sanctifies their privations to their highest good.

entries.title: II Kings 8:2
segments: The land of the Philistines; on the Mediterranean, south-west of Canaan.

entries.title: II Kings 8:6
segments: The goodness of God is often manifested towards his people, by inclining those in authority to do them justice and show them favor.

entries.title: II Kings 8:8
segments:
Hazael; an officer of the king of Syria. 
 
Men who in health pay no regard to God or his people, in sickness or distress often apply to them for help.

entries.title: II Kings 8:10
segments:
Thou mayest--recover; his disease was not in itself mortal, and would not cause his death. 
 
  He shall surely die; because, as the event showed, Hazael would kill him.  Such is the common, and perhaps the preferable interpretation of this passage.  But the original Hebrew text may be read, Go, say unto him, Thou shalt surely not recover; for the Lord hath showed me that he shall surely die.  According to this reading, Hazael directly falsified the prophet's words.  According to the common interpretation, he suppressed the second part of them. 
 
Of many blessings which God would otherwise bestow, men are often deprived by the wickedness of their fellow men.

entries.title: II Kings 8:11
segments:
He settled his countenance; on Hazeal. 
 
  Until he was ashamed; till Hazael was put out of countenance. 
 
  Wept; foreseeing the cruelties Hazael would commit.

entries.title: II Kings 8:13
segments:
But what, is thy serant a dog;probably meaning, What is thy servant, who is but a dog?  that is, a man in a very humble position. 
 
  This great thing; a work which could be performed only by one invested with royal power. 
 
A change of circumstances often shows that men are much more wicked than they imagined, and that nothing but the grace of God keeps them from the commission of the most enormous crimes.

entries.title: II Kings 8:14
segments: Thou shouldest surely recover; see note to

. 
 
A slight change in the words of a communication may entirely alter its meaning, and convey to the hearers a false impression.

entries.title: II Kings 8:18
segments: A man's character and conduct are greatly influenced by his wife; and no one should marry a woman who will draw him away from the service of God.

entries.title: II Kings 8:21
segments: Smote the Edomites which compassed him about; this seems to have been not so much a decisive victory on the part of Jehoram, as an escape from destruction.  Hence it is added in the next verse that the revolt of the Edomites was permanent.

entries.title: II Kings 8:22
segments: Libnah; one of the cities of Judah.

entries.title: II Kings 8:27
segments: The evil example of parents and those in authority may extend its mischievous influence not only to their children, but also to their distant posterity; and long after they are dead be instrumental in ruining their fellow men.

entries.title: II Kings 8:28
segments: Ramoth-gilead; east of Jordan, in the tribe of Gad.

entries.title: II Kings 8:29
segments:
Jezreel; west of the Jordan, in the tribe of Gad. 
 
  Ahaziah--went down; from Ramoth-gilead, whither he had gone in alliance with Joram.  Thus, by the providence of God, the king of Judah, being one of Ahab's descendants, was brought to Jezreel, to meet his death there with Joram at the hand of Jehu.
